# postino: MIME email over SMTP for D

postino is a library for the D programming language that builds MIME emails (plain text, HTML, embedded images, attachments) and sends them over SMTP through libcurl (`std.net.curl`), or saves them as `.eml` files. One class, `Email`, with chainable setters. Version 0.1.6, MIT license.

- Full reference: https://trikko.github.io/postino/llms-full.txt
- Rules for agents: https://trikko.github.io/postino/AGENTS.md (as a skill: https://trikko.github.io/postino/SKILL.md)
- API documentation: https://trikko.github.io/postino/
- Source: https://github.com/trikko/postino

## Core Concepts

- **Email**: `new Email()`, then chainable setters; every setter returns the same object.
- **Addresses**: `setFrom(address, name?)`, `addTo`, `addCc`, `addBcc`, `setReplyTo`. Checked when added: an invalid address throws at once. Bcc recipients receive the email and are never in the headers.
- **Content**: `setSubject`, `setPlainTextBody`, `setHtmlBody` (UTF-8, encoded for you: RFC 2047 headers, quoted-printable bodies).
- **Files**: `addAttachment(path, mimeType?, name?)` or `addAttachment(ubyte[] data, mimeType, name?)`; `addEmbeddedFile(path, cid, mimeType?)` or `addEmbeddedFile(ubyte[] data, cid, mimeType)`, shown in the HTML with `src="cid:..."`.
- **Sending**: `send(url, username?, password?, smtp?)`. `smtps://host:465` is implicit TLS; `smtp://host:587` with credentials requires STARTTLS; `smtp://host:25` without credentials is plain. Errors are exceptions.
- **Saving**: `save(path)` writes the same message as an `.eml` file, without sending it.

## Installation & Basic Usage

`dub add postino`. dmd or ldc2; libcurl at run time.

```d
import postino;

new Email()
    .setFrom("sender@example.com", "Sender")
    .addTo("alice@example.com", "Alice")
    .addBcc("archive@example.com")
    .setSubject("Hello")
    .setPlainTextBody("Hello Alice")
    .setHtmlBody("<p>Hello <b>Alice</b></p>")
    .addAttachment("/tmp/report.pdf")
    .send("smtp://smtp.example.com:587", "user", "password");
```

## Limits

Blocking, one connection per `send`. No DKIM, no custom headers, no templates, no OAuth2, no receiving mail. `smtps://` on port 587 does not work: 587 is `smtp://` with STARTTLS.
